1.week1: Inspect stored paddy for moisture — keep below 14% to prevent fungal growth.
1.week2: Clean and service the thresher before post-harvest processing.
1.week3: Apply mulch to harvested fields to conserve soil moisture for the next crop.
1.week4: Collect soil samples for testing — results guide your Kharif fertiliser plan.
alerts: Watch for rodent damage in grain storage
Low temperature can affect germination of nursery beds

2.week1: Deep plough the field to expose soil-borne pests to winter cold.
2.week2: Apply Farm Yard Manure (FYM) at 10 tonnes/ha and incorporate into soil.
2.week3: Check bunds and levelling — uneven fields waste 30% more irrigation water.
2.week4: Order certified seed for summer nursery if planning a June transplant.
alerts: Soil temperature still low — delay nursery sowing until March

3.week1: Prepare raised nursery beds (1m wide, 10m long) with well-drained soil.
3.week2: Treat seeds with Carbendazim 2g/kg to prevent seed-borne diseases.
3.week3: Sow pre-germinated seeds at 40g/m² for optimal seedling density.
3.week4: Apply light irrigation twice daily — avoid water stagnation in nursery.
alerts: Monitor for blast disease in nursery — apply Tricyclazole if spotted
Aphid infestation risk rising with warming temperatures

4.week1: Apply urea top-dressing at 5g/m² to nursery beds for vigorous seedling growth.
4.week2: Weed nursery beds manually — do not use herbicides at this stage.
4.week3: Thin out overcrowded seedlings to improve air circulation.
4.week4: Seedlings should be 20–25 days old (3–4 leaves) before transplanting.
alerts: Leaf folder moths active — use light traps to monitor population

5.week1: Transplant seedlings at 2–3 per hill, 20cm × 15cm spacing for Kharif varieties.
5.week2: Apply basal fertiliser: DAP 50kg/ha + MOP 40kg/ha before transplanting.
5.week3: Maintain 2–5cm standing water for the first 2 weeks after transplanting.
5.week4: Gap-fill any missing hills within 7 days of transplanting.
alerts: Stem borer active — apply Chlorpyrifos granules at transplanting
Check weather forecast — avoid transplanting just before heavy rain

6.week1: Apply first nitrogen split (urea 65 kg/ha) at 15 days after transplanting (DAT).
6.week3: Drain field for 3–4 days at tillering stage to strengthen root system.
6.week4: Scout for brown plant hopper (BPH) — check base of plants weekly.
alerts: Monsoon onset — risk of blast increases significantly
Zinc deficiency (yellowing leaves) — apply ZnSO4 at 25 kg/ha

7.week1: Apply second nitrogen split (urea 65 kg/ha) at 45 DAT.
7.week2: Maintain 5–8cm water level during active tillering.
7.week3: Pull out and destroy any Tungro-infected plants immediately.
7.week4: Install pheromone traps for stem borer monitoring (1 trap/ha).
alerts: High humidity — ideal conditions for Sheath Blight. Apply Validamycin if threshold exceeded
BPH outbreak risk peak month

8.week1: Apply potash top-dressing (MOP 20 kg/ha) to improve grain quality.
8.week2: Apply third urea split (urea 30 kg/ha) at panicle initiation stage.
8.week3: Ensure no water stress during panicle initiation — critical stage.
8.week4: Scout for false smut balls on panicles — remove and burn affected ones.
alerts: Neck blast is peak risk now — spray Tricyclazole 0.6g/L at boot stage
Avoid broad-spectrum pesticides to protect natural enemies of BPH

9.week1: Maintain 3–5cm water during flowering — drought stress reduces yield by 40%.
9.week2: Do NOT spray pesticides during flowering — protects pollinators.
9.week3: Scout for grain discolouration — sign of bacterial blight or false smut.
9.week4: Begin field drainage 10 days before expected harvest for efficient combine operation.
alerts: Cyclone watch — lash paddy bundles if storm predicted
Grain damage from sparrows rises at dough stage — use scare devices

10.week1: Harvest when 80–85% of grains are golden yellow — avoid over-maturity.
10.week2: Use combine harvester or self-help group thresher to reduce losses.
10.week3: Dry harvested paddy to 14% moisture before storage.
10.week4: Register at nearest paddy procurement centre before closing date.
alerts: Unseasonal rain — cover harvested crop with tarpaulin immediately
Price advisory: MSP for common paddy is ₹2,183/quintal (2025–26)

11.week1: Chop and incorporate straw residue — avoids burning and improves soil health.
11.week2: Apply Trichoderma viride to decompose stubble faster.
11.week3: Irrigate field lightly and sow green manure (Dhaincha) as rabi break crop.
11.week4: Clean and store all farm equipment before the dry season.
alerts: Stubble burning ban in force — violations attract ₹2,500 fine
Apply lime if soil pH < 5.5

12.week1: Apply gypsum (500 kg/ha) on alkaline soils for soil amendment.
12.week2: Renew Kisan Credit Card before expiry for next season credit.
12.week3: Attend local KVK (Krishi Vigyan Kendra) training sessions if available.
12.week4: Plan next Kharif crop — select variety based on Bloomsense disease heatmap.
alerts: Fog and low temperatures — protect nursery beds with polythene covers

1.week1: Apply first irrigation (CRI stage) if 20–25 days have passed since sowing.
1.week2: Apply second urea top-dressing (65 kg/ha) at first irrigation.
1.week3: Scout for yellow rust on upper leaves — apply Propiconazole if spotted.
1.week4: Check for aphid colonies at leaf tips — threshold is 10 aphids/tiller.
alerts: Yellow rust spore movement is high in January
Low temperature may delay tillering in late sown crops

2.week1: Apply third irrigation at tillering stage (40–45 DAS).
2.week2: Spray 2,4-D sodium salt for broad-leaf weed control.
2.week3: Apply second nitrogen split at tillering.
2.week4: Monitor for Karnal Bunt in areas with high humidity.
alerts: Aphid outbreak risk peaks in February
Frost warning — delay irrigation if frost predicted in next 48 hours

3.week1: Apply fourth irrigation at jointing stage.
3.week2: Scout for stem rust — warm and humid nights increase risk.
3.week3: Apply foliar micronutrients (Zinc + Boron) for grain quality.
3.week4: Remove volunteer plants of different varieties.
alerts: Hailstorm risk in North India — assess crop insurance coverage

4.week1: Apply fifth irrigation at booting stage — most critical irrigation.
4.week2: Do NOT apply nitrogen at this stage — will increase lodging risk.
4.week3: Monitor for aphids on ear heads — spray imidacloprid at threshold.
4.week4: Check for powdery mildew on upper leaves.
alerts: Unseasonal rain + high humidity — Scab (Fusarium head blight) risk elevated

5.week1: Apply sixth (final) irrigation at grain filling if available.
5.week2: Avoid any chemical spray — residue risk in grain.
5.week3: Estimate yield and contact local mandi for registration.
5.week4: Harvest when grains are fully dry and hard (< 12% moisture).
alerts: Hot dry winds (loo) accelerate maturity — may reduce grain weight

6.week3: Sell or store in jute bags.
alerts: MSP for wheat is ₹2,275/quintal (2025–26)
Soil moisture conservation critical in July

10.week4: Sow if soil temperature is below 25°C.

11.week1: Sow wheat in first fortnight of November for timely sown crop.
11.week2: Seed rate: 100 kg/ha for timely sown, 125 kg/ha for late sown.
11.week3: Apply basal dose: Urea 65kg + DAP 100kg + MOP 40kg per ha.
11.week4: First irrigation (pre-sowing) if soil moisture is low.
alerts: Delay in monsoon withdrawal may push sowing into late window — use late-sown varieties like PBW 373

12.week1: Ensure uniform germination — resow if < 70% germination.
12.week2: First irrigation at Crown Root Initiation (CRI) — 20–22 DAS.
12.week3: Scout for termite damage — apply Chlorpyrifos if needed.
12.week4: Remove weeds manually before first irrigation.
alerts: Fog may reduce sunlight — monitor for elongated, weak seedlings

1.week4: Apply Ca+Mg foliar to prevent BER.
alerts: Spider mites active in dry cold weather

2.week1: Avoid excess nitrogen at flowering stage.
2.week2: Install sticky traps for whitefly monitoring.
2.week3: Scout for Tomato Leaf Curl Virus (TLCV) — remove infected plants.
2.week4: Apply potassium foliar for fruit set.
alerts: TLCV spread by whitefly peaks in Feb-March

3.week3: Scout for fruit borer — apply biopesticide (HaNPV).
alerts: Price dips in March — consider cold-chain or processing options

4.week1: Pull out crop residue and destroy.
4.week2: Prepare nursery beds for Kharif tomato.
4.week4: Apply shade net on nursery to protect from heat.

5.week4: Apply mulch film to conserve moisture.
alerts: High rain — waterlogging is fatal. Ensure raised beds
Monsoon humidity — bacterial speck risk high
Late blight can destroy crop in 7 days — act immediately
Thrips and jassids — early action critical

7.week4: Apply growth regulator (Mepiquat Chloride) if vigorous.
alerts: Pink bollworm — most damaging pest of Bt cotton in India

9.week3: Apply foliar potash for boll opening.
9.week4: Sell at nearest CCI procurement centre.
alerts: MSP for medium staple cotton: ₹7,121/quintal (2025–26)

10.week2: Apply defoliant if late bolls not opening.
10.week3: Pull out stalks after last pick.
10.week4: Destroy stalks — reduces next season pest carryover.

alerts: Fall Armyworm — check whorls daily

7.week2: Scout for Fall Armyworm in whorls.
7.week3: Apply Emamectin Benzoate for FAW control.
alerts: FAW is the #1 threat to Kharif maize — inspect whorls every 3 days

8.week2: Detassel male plants in seed production plots.
8.week3: Ensure no water stress at silking.

9.week4: Harvest when husk is fully dry.

10.week4: Sell or store with hermetic bags.
alerts: MSP for Maize: ₹2,090/quintal (2025–26)

11.week1: Sow Rabi maize in irrigated conditions.

1.week1: Apply light irrigation during cold spell.
alerts: Frost warning in North India — keep soil moist

2.week1: Apply first top-dressing of urea (65 kg/ha).
alerts: Early shoot borer dead hearts — apply Fipronil or Trichocards

3.week2: Earthing up to support cane roots.
3.week3: Install light traps for borer moths.

4.week1: Increase irrigation frequency as temperature rises.
4.week2: Apply trash mulch to prevent moisture loss.
alerts: High evaporation — do not delay irrigation beyond 10 days

5.week1: Apply third split of nitrogen + MOP (40 kg/ha).
5.week3: Check drainage channels before pre-monsoon showers.

6.week1: Ensure zero waterlogging in cane furrows.
6.week2: Scout for red rot symptoms (red discolored pith).
6.week3: Propping / tying canes together to prevent lodging.
6.week4: Monitor for whitefly in humid pockets.
alerts: Red rot alert — uproot and burn infected stools immediately

7.week1: Maintain cane tying (trash twist) against high winds.
7.week2: Inspect upper leaves for sheath rot.
7.week3: Check rodent activity and apply zinc phosphide baits.
7.week4: Apply micronutrient mix if leaves pale.

8.week1: Check brix / sugar content of early planted crops.
8.week3: Scout for scale insects on lower nodes.
8.week4: Detrash dry lower leaves to improve sunlight penetration.

9.week1: Stop nitrogen application to maximize sucrose content.
9.week4: Coordinate with sugar mill for harvesting calendar.

10.week1: Harvest early varieties with hand cane cutter at ground level.
10.week2: Treat setts with Carbendazim (1g/L) for autumn planting.
10.week3: Plant setts in deep furrows with basal DAP.
10.week4: Transport harvested cane to mill within 24 hours.
alerts: FRP for Sugarcane is ₹340/quintal (2025–26)

11.week1: Cut canes flush with ground to encourage ratoon tillers.
11.week2: Apply stubble shaving and FYM to ratoon fields.
11.week4: Monitor sugar recovery rate at factory.

12.week2: Gap filling with polybag raised setts.
12.week3: Apply basal NPK to ratoon crop.

10.week2: Cut seed tubers with 2–3 eyes and treat with Mancozeb (2g/L).
alerts: Ensure well-sprouted disease-free certified seed tubers

11.week1: Apply first light irrigation at 10–12 days after planting.
11.week2: Weed and earth up when sprouts reach 15cm height.
11.week3: Apply first top-dressing of urea (45 kg/ha).
alerts: Aphids transmit leaf roll virus — monitor with yellow water traps

12.week1: Maintain optimal soil moisture — avoid dry spells.
12.week2: Second earthing up to ensure no tubers are exposed to sunlight.
12.week3: Apply second split of urea + SOP (Sulfate of Potash).
12.week4: Foliar spray of Mancozeb (2g/L) as prophylactic for blight.
alerts: Late blight risk high during foggy/cloudy cold weather

1.week1: Critical water stage — irrigate at 7–8 day intervals.
1.week2: Inspect foliage for Late Blight water-soaked lesions.
1.week3: Spray Cymoxanil + Mancozeb if blight symptoms seen.
1.week4: Apply potassium and boron foliar for smooth skin.
alerts: Late blight alert — can destroy crop in 48 hours in high humidity

2.week1: Stop irrigation 10–12 days prior to dehaulming.
2.week2: Cut off potato foliage (dehaulming) to harden tuber skin.
2.week3: Allow tubers to cure in soil for 10–14 days.
2.week4: Inspect tubers for scab or hollow heart.

3.week1: Harvest tubers on clear sunny days using potato digger.
3.week2: Cure harvested potatoes under shade for 10 days.
3.week3: Grade into seed, table, and processing sizes.
3.week4: Store in well-ventilated cool shed or cold storage.
alerts: Never expose freshly harvested tubers to direct harsh sunlight

4.week1: Clean storage bins and treat with CIPC sprout suppressant.
4.week2: Deep plough field to kill surviving soil fungi.
4.week3: Sow green manure crop (Sunn hemp / Dhaincha).

6.week3: Drain monsoon rain from fallow fields.

8.week1: Order seed tubers from certified sources.

9.week1: Remove seed potatoes from cold storage 2 weeks before sowing.
9.week2: Keep in diffused light for uniform green sprouting (chitting).
9.week4: Final field preparation with deep tilth.

6.week1: Sow with onset of monsoon (75–100mm rainfall received).
6.week2: Treat seeds with Rhizobium + PSB culture (10g/kg).
alerts: Do not sow in dry soil — ensure at least 4 inches moist profile

7.week1: Gap filling and thinning to maintain 30 plants/m².
7.week2: First hand weeding or interculture at 20 DAS.
7.week3: Scout for Girdle Beetle and Semilooper caterpillars.
7.week4: Apply Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 0.3ml/L if pests seen.
alerts: Girdle beetle active — spray when 5% ring cut plants observed

8.week1: Ensure no moisture stress during flowering — critical yield phase.
8.week2: Foliar spray of 19:19:19 (1%) for flower retention.
8.week3: Scout for Yellow Mosaic Virus (transmitted by whitefly).
8.week4: Spray Thiamethoxam 25% WG @ 0.3g/L for whitefly control.
alerts: Yellow Mosaic Virus alert — uproot infected yellow plants immediately

9.week1: Foliar spray of 00:52:34 (1%) to boost grain bolding.
9.week3: Monitor pod color transition from green to golden brown.
9.week4: Harvest when 90% of leaves drop and pods turn brown.
alerts: MSP for Soybean: ₹4,892/quintal (2025–26)

10.week1: Harvest early morning to prevent pod shattering losses.
10.week2: Thresh at low cylinder speed (400–500 RPM) to protect seed embryo.
10.week3: Dry seed to 10–12% moisture before bagging.
10.week4: Sell at designated APMC mandi or store in hermetic bags.

11.week1: Deep plough fields and sow Rabi chickpea or wheat.
11.week2: Incorporate soybean residue into soil for organic nitrogen.
11.week3: Store seed stocks in cool dry room.

12.week3: Seed viability test for saved seeds.

3.week1: Deep summer ploughing to destroy pest pupae.

1.week1: Protect bunches from cold with perforated plastic covers.
1.week3: Remove dried and diseased lower leaves.
alerts: Cold injury alert — irrigate at night to keep soil warm

2.week2: Desuckering — remove side suckers to direct energy to main stem.
2.week3: Earthing up to cover exposed roots.

3.week2: Inject monocrotophos/neem oil for stem borer.
3.week3: Ensure drip system emitter flow is uniform.
3.week4: Propping with bamboo poles for shooting trees.

4.week1: Remove male bud (denavelling) after all hands have opened.
4.week2: Cover bunch with blue polythene sleeve for uniform color.
4.week4: Increase water supply during fruit filling.

5.week1: Apply sulfate of potash (SOP) for sweet fruit pulp.
5.week2: Propping heavy bunches against summer storm winds.
5.week4: Keep field free of weed competition.
alerts: Pre-monsoon gale winds — prop bunches with double bamboo

6.week1: Ensure quick drainage — banana roots rot in waterlogged soil.
6.week2: Apply Trichoderma viride to prevent Panama wilt.
6.week3: Foliar spray of Propiconazole (1ml/L) against Sigatoka.
6.week4: Harvest mature bunches with angular to round ribs.
alerts: Sigatoka leaf spot outbreaks peak in monsoon humidity

7.week2: Spray mineral oil + fungicide for leaf spot.
7.week3: Plant new tissue culture saplings in deep pits.
7.week4: Apply FYM 20kg + 500g neem cake per plant.

8.week2: Apply first dose of NPK for new crop.
8.week3: Harvest mature crops and pack with foam separators.
8.week4: Remove older harvested mother pseudostem safely.

9.week3: Monitor for banana aphid (vector for bunchy top virus).
9.week4: Grade and pack bananas in CFB boxes for export.
alerts: Bunchy top virus alert — eradicate infected plants immediately

11.week3: Check drip drippers for salt blockage.

12.week2: Night irrigation during severe cold waves.

1.week2: Withhold irrigation during flower bud differentiation.
1.week3: Scout for mango hopper at panicle base.
1.week4: Do NOT spray pesticides during peak bloom (protect bee pollinators).
alerts: Mango hopper and powdery mildew attack peaks during panicle bloom

2.week1: Maintain honey bee hives in orchard for cross-pollination.
2.week2: Avoid chemical spraying during daytime flowering.
2.week3: Inspect for powdery mildew white powdery coating.
2.week4: Apply sulfur dust if mildew spotted at night.
alerts: Cloudy weather during bloom causes severe fruit drop

3.week1: Resume irrigation as fruits reach pea size.
3.week2: Spray Planofix (NAA 20ppm) to prevent early fruit drop.
3.week3: Apply foliar Boron (0.1%) + Zinc (0.2%) for fruit retention.

4.week2: Install methyl eugenol pheromone traps for fruit fly (6 traps/ha).
4.week3: Spray potassium nitrate (1%) to boost fruit sizing.
4.week4: Scout for mango nut weevil and anthracnose.
alerts: Fruit fly attack begins — hang pheromone traps in all quadrants

5.week1: Harvest fruits with 8mm stalk attached using mango harvesters.
5.week2: Avoid direct ground drops to prevent skin bruising.
5.week3: Hot water treatment (48°C for 20 min) against fruit fly/anthracnose.
5.week4: Grade by size and pack in ventilated CFB cartons.
alerts: Never use calcium carbide for ripening — illegal and harmful

6.week1: Complete harvest of late varieties (Mallika, Amrapali, Dasheri).
6.week2: Post-harvest pruning: remove dead, diseased and criss-cross branches.
6.week3: Apply Bordeaux paste (10%) on cut wound surfaces.
6.week4: Apply heavy irrigation and FYM (50kg/tree) after pruning.

7.week1: Apply full annual dose of FYM + Phosphorus + Potash in root trench.
7.week2: Ensure tree basin has no standing water.
7.week3: Spray Copper Oxychloride (3g/L) to prevent anthracnose and dieback.
7.week4: Plant cover crops (Cowpea) in orchard interspaces.
alerts: Waterlogging causes root asphyxiation — drain excess monsoon water

8.week1: New coppery-red shoot flush emerges — monitor for leaf gall midge.
8.week2: Spray Dimethoate (1.5ml/L) if leaf webber or gall midge appears.
8.week3: Incorporate intercropped green manure into soil.
8.week4: Clean trunk bases and apply lime wash.

9.week1: Center-opening pruning to allow sunlight inside inner canopy.
9.week2: Remove rootstock sprouts (water suckers) from grafted trees.
9.week3: Apply Paclobutrazol (Cultar) on alternate bearing mature trees.
9.week4: Inspect trunks for stem borer exit holes and frass.
alerts: Treat stem borer holes with kerosene/dichlorvos and seal with mud

10.week1: Stop all nitrogen applications to encourage shoot maturity.
10.week3: Paint tree trunks with white lime + Copper sulfate (1kg:100g in 10L).
10.week4: Scout for red rust algae on mature leaves.

11.week1: Strictly withhold irrigation to induce flower bud formation.
11.week2: Clear dry leaves and prune water shoots.

12.week1: Clean orchard floor completely to remove overwintering hoppers.
12.week2: Check spray equipment for upcoming flowering season.
12.week4: Inspect swollen buds for first panicle emergence.
alerts: Cold wave warning — light smudge smoke in orchard on freezing nights

10.week1: Prepare raised nursery beds and treat seed with Thiram (2g/kg).
10.week2: Sow seeds in lines 5cm apart at 8–10 kg/ha.
10.week3: Light irrigation daily until uniform germination.
10.week4: Drench nursery with Trichoderma against damping-off.
alerts: Damping-off risk high — avoid excess watering of nursery beds

11.week1: Harden 45-day old seedlings by withholding water for 3 days.
11.week2: Dip seedling roots in Carbendazim solution before planting.
11.week3: Transplant at 15cm × 10cm on flat beds or broad beds.

12.week1: Apply first top-dressing of urea (35 kg/ha) at 30 DAT.
12.week4: Scout for Onion Thrips (silvery patches on leaves).
alerts: Thrips infestation peaks in dry weather — spray Fipronil or Neem oil

1.week1: Apply second split of urea (35 kg/ha) + Potassium sulfate (25 kg/ha).
1.week2: Apply sulfur (25 kg/ha) for bulb pungency and storage quality.
1.week3: Scout for Purple Blotch disease (purple-brown spots).
alerts: Purple blotch destroys leaf area rapidly — spray at first spot appearance

2.week1: Critical water stage — irrigate at 6–8 day intervals.
2.week2: Do NOT apply nitrogen now (causes thick necks and poor storage).
2.week3: Foliar spray of 00:00:50 (1%) for bulb enlargement.
2.week4: Check for basal rot in damp soil pockets.

3.week1: Stop irrigation 10–15 days before harvest when 50% tops fall.
3.week2: Allow tops to dry completely in the field.
3.week3: Harvest bulbs by pulling manually on dry sunny days.
3.week4: Field cure under shade with leaves covering bulbs for 3–5 days.
alerts: Harvesting too early causes rotting; harvesting too late causes splitting

4.week1: Cut dry foliage leaving 2.5cm neck on the bulb.
4.week2: Grade by diameter: Small, Medium (40–60mm), Large.
4.week3: Discard thick-necked, double or bruised bulbs.
4.week4: Store in ventilated bamboo onion chawls at < 70% humidity.
alerts: Never heap onions higher than 3–4 feet to prevent suffocation rot

5.week1: Inspect stored onions weekly for sprouting or rot.
5.week2: Ensure continuous air circulation in storage shed.
5.week3: Prepare land for Kharif onion nursery.
5.week4: Procure Kharif varieties (Bhima Super, AgriFound Dark Red).

6.week1: Sow Kharif nursery on raised beds with shade nets.

9.week3: Immediate marketing (Kharif onions don't store long).
9.week4: Prepare nursery for main Rabi crop.

6.week1: Sow seeds in protrays with cocopeat + Trichoderma.
6.week2: Cover with 50% white shade net to protect from rain.
6.week3: Harden 30-day old seedlings before field planting.
6.week4: Prepare main field ridges at 60cm spacing with basal NPK.
alerts: Damping off risk high — drench with Copper Oxychloride (2.5g/L)

7.week1: Transplant seedlings at 60cm × 45cm spacing on ridges.
7.week2: Apply drip irrigation and silver-black mulch film.
7.week3: Dip roots in Pseudomonas fluorescens solution before planting.

8.week1: First top-dressing of urea (40 kg/ha) + micronutrient foliar spray.
8.week2: Install blue sticky traps for thrips and yellow for whiteflies.
8.week3: Scout for Chilli Murda (Leaf curl caused by thrips/mites).
8.week4: Spray Diafenthiuron 50% WP @ 1.2g/L if upward leaf curling seen.
alerts: Chilli leaf curl thrips alert — spray underside of leaves thoroughly

9.week1: Apply Planofix (NAA 10ppm) at flowering to prevent flower drop.
alerts: Anthracnose causes circular sunken lesions on ripe pods — spray early

10.week1: Harvest tender green chillies at 10–12 day intervals.
10.week2: Grade and pack in ventilated crates for local market.
10.week3: Continue fertigation with calcium nitrate and boron.

11.week1: Allow selected chillies to turn deep red for dry chilli market.
11.week2: Spray neem oil 1500ppm to deter late season sucking pests.
11.week3: Apply MOP (Potash) to enhance red capsaicin color.
11.week4: Harvest first flush of fully ripe red fruits.

12.week1: Harvest deep red ripe pods manually.
12.week2: Dry on clean cement threshing floor or solar tunnel dryer.
12.week3: Dry to 10% moisture (pods should give rattling seed sound).
12.week4: Separate damaged, discolored or stalkless chillies.
alerts: Never dry chillies directly on bare mud floor (causes aflatoxin)

1.week1: Irrigate crop after each major picking.
1.week2: Apply light nitrogen + potash boost for next flush.
1.week3: Dry second flush of red pods.
1.week4: Bag dried chillies in gunny bags lined with polythene.

2.week3: Scout for powdery mildew in late winter.
2.week4: Grade by size and pungent grade.

3.week1: Final harvest of remaining green and red pods.
3.week2: Pull out old exhausted chilli bushes.
3.week3: Deep plough field to expose root-knot nematode eggs.
3.week4: Incorporate FYM and sow summer green manure.

4.week1: Solarize soil using clear polythene film.
4.week2: Clean and store dried chilli bags in cold store (4–6°C).
4.week3: Check market rates on e-NAM / Spices Board.

5.week1: Procure certified seeds (G4, Teja, Byadgi, Pusa Jwala).
